correctness.rationale: The two unimodular child maps descend to P¹(F_p) as r/(r+1) and r+1, with homogeneous interpretation at poles. Inversion swaps the children and fixes the root, giving the stated equalities of class counts. Direct transition counting gives the updates (A+C,2A,2B) and (U+X,2U,V+W,2W). Starting with only class 1 present, the ternary depth-3 and depth-4 vectors are (2,4,0) and (2,4,8); the quinary ones are (2,0,1,2) and (4,4,1,2). No earlier row is complete, since each coordinate has at least one positive incoming transition in the reduced updates, so completeness persists. Solving the updates in formal series yields the supplied rational functions. For both matrices, the constant class vector has eigenvalue 2; its component is fixed by the total count 2^n with multiplicities of the inversion classes. The other roots are (−1±i√7)/2 in the ternary case, and −1 and (1±i√7)/2 in the quinary case. Roots are distinct; both conjugate pairs have modulus √2. Matching initial vectors against the induced scalar recurrences gives the complex coefficients −1/8+5i/(8√7) and i√7/14 for the zero classes and the additional −(−1)^n/6 at five. For either phase θ, 2cos(2θ)=−3/2 cannot be a rational algebraic integer, so the rotations are irrational and dense even on every tail. Thus the normalized extrema are ±2 times the respective coefficient moduli, including the infinity class by inversion. The other classes have the uniform order bound, not a claim of tabulated amplitudes for them.
residual_risks: The frozen regression code was inspected, not replayed. It records exact direct rows through 15 and formal-series coefficients through 80, not an infinite proof; the rotation and spectral arguments establish the infinite claim.
